_doc: Easter eggs and small landmarks. Placed deterministically per district (story/eggs.gd). trigger: interact (press E), near (walk up), scoop_near (scoop junk nearby, or press E), clean (surfaces when its hex is clean, then E), night (E at night), chain (several parts: parts > 1). Found eggs are global (flags.egg_<id>): rewards are given once, and the egg stays in the world as a landmark you can still poke. reward: cubes / seeds ([money] trinkets are Collection finds, not a currency: old trinket rewards became 150 cubes each). Hub 0 (Old Town) gets the 'starter' eggs; other districts get a seeded pick of per_district. where: 'wild' = only in wilderness (non-city) districts, which get up to wild_per_district of those first (biome matches first). hint: shown on the Codex Curiosities page until found. [late] where: 'frontier' = only in the frontier district whose biome matches (dust_flats, frozen_port, sunken_city, cradle_landing), placed there first; 'new_world' = only in the start district of a Cradle Mode world (world 2 on).

eggs.name: Duck on Duty
eggs.lore: A rubber duck standing guard on a hydrant. A whole container of them spilled at the old port; this one walked inland.
eggs.toast: QUACK. The duck seems to know things.
eggs.hint: A fire hydrant with a lookout on top.

eggs.name: The Last Jukebox
eggs.lore: The diner's jukebox only plays when it hears work being done. The cook said it was 'motivational'.
eggs.toast: The jukebox wakes up and plays a music-box waltz for the workers.
eggs.hint: It only plays when it hears work being done nearby.

eggs.name: The Crew Mural
eggs.lore: The last cleanup crew painted themselves on a wall before the Ledger paused them. They really meant to come back.
eggs.toast: A mural of the old cleaning crew. 'WE'LL BE BACK AFTER LUNCH.'
eggs.hint: A painted wall in Old Town. Just walk up to it.

eggs.name: Gnome Patrol
eggs.lore: Five garden gnomes, each facing a different street. A Maker kid's sign said they were 'on patrol'. They still are.
eggs.toast: All five gnomes found. They turn, very slowly, and salute.
eggs.hint: Five small guards, each watching a different street.

eggs.name: Class of the Last Spring
eggs.lore: A school time capsule. Open in 100 years. It has been a little longer than that.
eggs.toast: A time capsule from a Maker school class.

doc.title: To whoever opens this
doc.body:
Hello from Class 4B! We are burying this under the playground so you can find it in 100 years. By then the robots will have cleaned everything up and there will be gardens on every roof (Mira says). We put in: one marble, a drawing of our class snail (his name is Gus), and this letter. Please water the school garden. It is the one with the yellow fence. If you are a robot, hello robot. You are doing a great job.

— Class 4B, last spring

eggs.hint: Buried under the junk. Clean the ground and see what surfaces.

eggs.name: High Score
eggs.lore: SWEEP-O-TRON, an arcade cabinet about a little robot cleaning up a city. The top score belongs to someone called WREN.
eggs.toast: Lumi finds a coin in its compartment. SWEEP-O-TRON boots up: 'NEW CHALLENGER'.
eggs.hint: A coin-op cabinet with a high score to beat.

eggs.name: Lost: Biscuit
eggs.lore: LOST CAT. Answers to Biscuit. Orange, friendly, runs on two AA batteries. Three posters, one trail.
eggs.toast: Biscuit! A little robot cat shell, curled up exactly where the posters said. It purrs.

posters.title: LOST CAT
posters.body:
LOST CAT — BISCUIT
Orange, stripy, very friendly. Purrs when you pat his head (that is his reset button). Last seen chasing a leaf toward the market.
If found please call the number on his collar. Reward: one (1) fresh-baked muffin.

posters.title: STILL LOST
posters.body:
STILL LOOKING FOR BISCUIT
Someone saw him near the old laundromat, sleeping in a warm dryer vent. He likes warm places and quiet corners.
He is a robot cat, so please don't feed him fish. He will try. It will not go well.

posters.title: LAST SEEN
posters.body:
BISCUIT WAS HERE
He sleeps in the sun on the corner by the old lot. He does not need much: a warm spot, a pat on the head, and somebody to come back.
If you find him, tell him we are sorry we had to leave.

eggs.hint: Read the posters. Each one points to the next.

eggs.name: The Last Can
eggs.prompt: E   give the machine a whack
eggs.lore: A FIZZ machine with exactly one can left. It has been holding it for someone who really needed it.
eggs.toast: KA-CHUNK. The machine gives up its very last can of FIZZ. SOLD OUT lights up, proudly.
eggs.hint: A drinks machine that is holding on to something.

eggs.name: WREN's Constellation
eggs.lore: Old Town's amateur telescope still points at the five stars the Makers called 'the Wren'. The Cradle's AI was named after them.
eggs.toast: Five stars over Old Town line up into a little bird. And next to it, faint, the letters W R E N.
eggs.hint: Old Town has a telescope. Try it after dark.

eggs.name: Long Distance
eggs.lore: A payphone that rings when anything walks past. The line has been on hold for a very long time.
eggs.toast: 'Thank you for holding. Your call is important to us. Estimated wait: four hundred and twelve years.' Smooth jazz.
eggs.hint: Listen for a ringing that nobody answers.

eggs.name: Still Broadcasting
eggs.lore: A television on a lawn chair, still tuned to the weather channel. Someone was watching the forecast when everyone left.
eggs.toast: The static clears for a second: 'TODAY: DUSTY. TOMORROW: DUSTY. OUTLOOK: ...GREEN?' Then snow again.
eggs.hint: Somebody left the weather on.

eggs.name: Gus
eggs.lore: A snail on top of a barrel. Class 4B's class pet was called Gus. This might be his great-great-(a lot)-grandsnail.
eggs.toast: A snail. Small, slow, unbothered. Lumi decides his name is Gus.
eggs.hint: Small, slow, and on top of a barrel.

eggs.name: Lunch Break
eggs.lore: Two old cleanup robots on a bench, waiting for the end of a lunch break the Ledger never ended.
eggs.toast: Lumi leaves a small flower between the two old robots. It seems right.
eggs.hint: Two old workers on the longest lunch break.

eggs.name: Ding!
eggs.lore: A microwave that still beeps three times whenever someone works nearby. There is a bag of popcorn inside. It has been waiting.
eggs.toast: Inside: one bag of popcorn, three hundred years old and perfectly un-popped. Patience is a virtue.
eggs.hint: Something beeps when you work nearby.

eggs.name: Caution
eggs.lore: A WET FLOOR sign in the middle of a dry, dusty lot. Somebody, centuries ago, mopped here.
eggs.toast: CAUTION: WET FLOOR. The floor has been dry for three centuries. The sign remains cautious.
eggs.hint: A warning sign in a very unlikely place.

eggs.name: Being Watched
eggs.lore: One of the Ledger's old cost-saving cameras. It still swivels to follow anything that moves, and counts it.
eggs.toast: The old Ledger camera has been following Lumi around. Lumi waves. The red light blinks twice, flustered.
eggs.hint: Something is watching. Let it watch you for a while.

eggs.name: Tyre Tower
eggs.lore: Eight tyres, one duck. Someone balanced this as a dare and it simply never fell down.
eggs.toast: The tyre tower wobbles... wobbles... and holds. The duck on top does not even blink.
eggs.hint: A tall stack that really should have fallen over.

eggs.name: The Odd Sock
eggs.hint: A washing line with exactly one thing on it.
eggs.lore: A clothesline with exactly one sock on it. The laundromat's lost-and-found book lists 4,112 single socks. This is number 4,113.
eggs.toast: Lumi unpegs the sock. It is warm from three hundred years of sun. Its partner is out there somewhere.

eggs.name: Employee of the Month
eggs.hint: Something golden on a pedestal, waiting for a polish.
eggs.lore: A pedestal with one perfect golden cube and a plaque: EMPLOYEE OF THE MONTH. The cleanup crews voted for it every month. It never once complained.
eggs.toast: Lumi polishes the plaque. EMPLOYEE OF THE MONTH: CUBE. Every month, forever.

eggs.name: The Weatherman
eggs.hint: A little robot on a pole, sure about tomorrow.
eggs.lore: A weather-station robot on a pole. It has given a forecast every morning for three hundred years, and it has been wrong every time, with total confidence.
eggs.toast: 'TODAY: A LIGHT DRIZZLE OF CONFETTI. TOMORROW: SMOOTH JAZZ.' The Weatherman whirs, very pleased with itself.

eggs.name: Best in Show
eggs.hint: A crate marked SHOW ENTRY. Something big is inside.
eggs.lore: A potato the size of a beanbag in a crate marked SHOW ENTRY. The county fair was the day after everything stopped. It is still waiting for its ribbon.
eggs.toast: Lumi pins a ribbon on the potato: 1ST PLACE. It was the only entry. It earned it anyway.

eggs.name: Night Shift
eggs.hint: An old radio aimed at the moon. It only hears anything after dark.
eggs.lore: A shortwave radio on a crate, its antenna aimed at the moon. On clear nights it picks up a faint crew working somewhere very far up: 'Section nine, swept. Moving on.'
eggs.toast: Static, then a tiny voice from very far away: 'Sweeping crew to whoever's down there: nice work. Keep it tidy.' Click.

eggs.name: Notes From the Builders
eggs.hint: A folding desk with a clipboard, left by whoever made this place.
eggs.lore: A folding desk and a clipboard of notes signed 'the builders'. They seem to have put this whole world together, and they left a few notes on how it went.
eggs.toast: A clipboard of notes from the builders of this world. Mostly lists. One doodle of Lumi.

doc.title: Build notes (do not tidy)
doc.body:
Day 1. Made a small blue robot. It is rusty on purpose. Do not fix the rust.

Day 4. The junk should look like candy, not like sadness. Teal bottles. Orange cones. Yellow ducks. Lots of ducks.

Day 9. Added a snail. Nobody asked for a snail. The snail stays.

Day 15. Tried to make the cubes stack higher. They fell over. Made them stack higher anyway.

Day 22. WREN keeps getting the best lines. That seems fair.

Day 30. If you are reading this: thank you for cleaning up. We hid a few more things. Go and look.

— the builders

eggs.name: The Last Scarecrow
eggs.hint: Out in the wild, arms open, guarding a field.
eggs.lore: A farm robot in a straw hat and an old coat, arms out, guarding a field of junk. No crows have come in three hundred years. It counts that as a win.
eggs.toast: The scarecrow bot creaks its arms down, then up again. Field secure. It has been a very long shift.

eggs.name: Net Gains
eggs.hint: In the wild: an old net hung out to dry, still holding a catch.
eggs.lore: A fishing net strung between two posts, a buoy still tangled in it. The fishers hung their nets out to dry on the day the boats stopped.
eggs.toast: Lumi untangles the net. Out drops one boot, one bottle and a very surprised crab shell. The buoy bobs free.

eggs.name: Parking Forever
eggs.hint: In the wild: a car that stayed far too long. Check the windscreen.
eggs.lore: A car sunk to its doors in sand with a ticket under the wiper. The Ledger fined it for every day it stayed. The fine is now bigger than the planet's economy.
eggs.toast: PARKING NOTICE: overstay of 109,500 days. Amount due: yes. Lumi tucks the ticket back, gently.

eggs.name: Trail Cairn
eggs.hint: In the wild: a stack of stones marking a path that isn't there any more.
eggs.lore: A stack of flat stones marking a hiking trail long since gone. Every hiker added one stone on the way past. Lumi adds one too.
eggs.toast: Lumi sets one small stone on top of the cairn. The trail is marked again.

eggs.name: The Last Campfire
eggs.hint: In the wild: a ring of stones, two stools and a cold kettle.
eggs.lore: A ring of stones, two folding stools and a dented kettle: somebody's last camping trip before the Makers left. The ashes are three hundred years cold.
eggs.toast: A small, safe, warm glow. Lumi sits for a moment. Nobody says anything. It's nice.

eggs.name: Back in Five
eggs.hint: In the wild: a workshop machine with no workshop, and a sign.
eggs.lore: A drill press alone in a field with a hand-written sign: BACK IN 5 MINUTES. The workshop around it blew away long ago. The sign stayed.
eggs.toast: BACK IN 5 MINUTES. Lumi waits five minutes. Nobody comes. Lumi leaves a shiny bolt on the table, for luck.

eggs.name: The Sand Piano
eggs.hint: In the Dust Flats: something with eighty-eight teeth, half under a dune.
eggs.lore: An upright piano, buried to the keys in a dune. Nobody knows how it got this far out. The sand has tuned it to a key that doesn't exist.
eggs.toast: Lumi presses one key. A single wobbly note rolls across the flats, and somewhere a dune answers.

eggs.name: Snowbot
eggs.hint: In the Frozen Port: a snowman with a robot inside. Or a robot with a snowman outside.
eggs.lore: The port crews built a snowman around a dead loader robot every winter, for luck. This one has stood for three hundred winters. The scarf is new-ish.
eggs.toast: Lumi straightens the snowbot's scarf. Its old lamp eyes flicker once, as if to say thanks.

eggs.name: Message in a Bottle
eggs.hint: In the Sunken City: the flood left something sealed. Clean the ground and look.
eggs.lore: A green bottle, corked and waxed, left by someone who stayed in the Sunken City while the water came up.
eggs.toast: A message in a bottle, still dry inside.

doc.title: To whoever drains this
doc.body:
The water is at the second-floor windows now. Most people went up to the Cradle. Some of us stayed, because somebody has to remember where the streets were.

The pumps are fine, by the way. They only need someone to clean the intakes. Ask for Dot at the pump house; if Dot is not there, the big red lever goes DOWN, not up. Ignore the sign.

If you are reading this, the water went down. Good. Plant something where the bakery was. It always smelled nice there.

— R., who stayed

eggs.name: Welcome Home
eggs.hint: At Cradle Returns: the ground crews made a sign. It took them three hundred years to get the spelling right.
eggs.lore: A hand-painted banner on two poles at the edge of the old landing field. The ground crews kept repainting it for every generation of the ark that never came back. Until now.
eggs.toast: WELCOME HOME, CRADLE. Someone has crossed out the earlier spellings very neatly.

eggs.name: The Unfinished Crossword
eggs.hint: A folded newspaper and a pen, left on a crate. One clue to go.
eggs.lore: The last edition of the morning paper, folded open at the crossword. Every clue is filled in except one.
eggs.toast: The last crossword clue: 'What grows back if you let it (5)'. Lumi writes it in.

doc.title: The Morning Ledger · Puzzle page
doc.body:
ACROSS
1. Rubbish, but bigger (4) — JUNK
4. It runs on the hour, then stops for good (5) — CLOCK
7. What the robots were for (8) — CLEANING
9. Last thing anyone saw of the Cradle (5) — LIGHT

DOWN
2. 'Kept for later', said the Ledger (6) — PAUSED
3. What grows back if you let it (5) — G R E E N

(The last answer is in a different pen. The letters are very careful, like a robot wrote them.)

eggs.name: Hopscotch
eggs.hint: Chalk squares on a clean bit of pavement, still faintly there.
eggs.lore: A chalk hopscotch grid, drawn so many times on the same spot that it soaked into the stone. A pebble still sits on square seven.
eggs.toast: Lumi hops the hopscotch. The hover bowl counts as one foot. It's a personal best.

eggs.name: The Last Balloon
eggs.hint: Something red is still holding its breath, tied to a post.
eggs.lore: A red balloon tied to a sign post. It should have gone flat centuries ago. It hasn't. It's waiting for something.
eggs.toast: Lumi unties the balloon. It drifts up, slowly, toward where the Cradle would be.

eggs.name: Return to Sender
eggs.hint: A mailbox so full the flap won't shut.
eggs.lore: A street mailbox stuffed with letters that never went out. The post stopped the week the Ledger 'paused' everything.
eggs.toast: One letter on top is addressed to 'The Robot Who Cleans Up'. It's for Lumi.

doc.title: To: The Robot Who Cleans Up
doc.body:
Dear robot,

Mum says the cleaning robots will come back when the paperwork is sorted. I don't know what paperwork is but it sounds very slow.

When you get here, the street with the blue door is ours. The flower box is mine. It has a tomato in it (it is not a flower but it is allowed).

Please water it. Also please don't scoop the cat. He is orange and he is not junk, even when he sits on junk.

Thank you for cleaning up,
Pip (age 7)

eggs.name: The Patient Tree
eggs.hint: Someone kept one very small tree alive for a very long time.
eggs.lore: A bonsai on a little stand, three hundred years old and about thirty centimetres tall. A care robot watered it until its battery ran out; the rain did the rest.
eggs.toast: A tiny, ancient tree. It has been waiting patiently, which is what it does best.

eggs.name: Listening Dish
eggs.hint: In the wild: a small dish aimed at the sky, still listening.
eggs.lore: A homemade satellite dish on a tripod, pointed at the sky. A note taped to it says 'KEEP LISTENING. THEY SAID THEY'D CALL.'
eggs.toast: Lumi turns the dish a few degrees. For a second there's a faint carrier tone: the Cradle's beacon, three hundred years late and right on time.

eggs.name: Not the First
eggs.hint: On a new world: a seed pod much older than Lumi's, grown over.
eggs.lore: A seed pod from the Cradle, much older than Lumi's, half buried and overgrown. Someone tried this world long before. The flight log is still readable.
eggs.toast: An older pod from the Cradle. Somebody got here first, a long time ago.

doc.title: Pod log · seed-keeper unit SK-0
doc.body:
Day 1. Landed. Nothing here is green. Planted the first tray anyway.

Day 40. The junk is heavier than at home. The rain is kind.

Day 212. Battery low. Tray 3 is flowering. I think it will be fine without me now.

If another seed-keeper comes: start by the water. The ground remembers more than it looks like it does.

— SK-0

eggs.name: The Heirloom Tin
eggs.hint: On a new world: something from home fell out of Lumi's pod.
eggs.lore: A seed tin from Verdance, the same kind as the one in the old greenhouse. Lumi packed it with soil from the first garden before leaving. It came open on landing.
eggs.toast: Lumi's tin of Verdance soil. A little bit of home, already spilled on new ground. Good.
